title: Ecclesiastes Bible Quiz - Chapter 2
description: Ten questions on Ecclesiastes 2: the Preacher's test of pleasure, his great works and riches, wisdom and folly, and eating and drinking from God's hand.

questions.text: What did the Preacher say in his heart he would test himself with?
questions.explanation: He said in his heart: 'Come now, I will test you with mirth: therefore enjoy pleasure,' and behold, this also was vanity.

answers.text: Mirth
Fasting
Hard labor
Silence

questions.text: Which of these great works did the Preacher make for himself?
questions.explanation: He says he built himself houses, planted vineyards, and made gardens and parks with all kinds of fruit trees.

answers.text: Temples and altars of stone
Walls and towers for the city
Ships and harbors by the sea
Houses, vineyards, gardens and parks

questions.text: Why did the Preacher make himself pools of water?
questions.explanation: He made himself pools of water to water from it the forest where trees were grown.

answers.text: To wash himself in them every day
To water the forest where trees were grown
To keep fish in them for his table
To give drink to his herds and flocks

questions.text: Besides silver and gold, what did the Preacher gather for himself?
questions.explanation: He gathered silver and gold and the treasure of kings and of the provinces, and got himself male and female singers and musical instruments of all sorts.

answers.text: Chariots and swift horses
Spices and rare perfumes
Singers and musical instruments
Weapons and armor for war

questions.text: What did the Preacher do with whatever his eyes desired?
questions.explanation: He says: whatever my eyes desired, I didn't keep from them; I didn't withhold my heart from any joy.

answers.text: He gave it to the poor
He weighed it with wisdom first
He turned his eyes away
He didn't keep it from them

questions.text: How far does wisdom excel folly, according to this chapter?
questions.explanation: He saw that wisdom excels folly, as far as light excels darkness.

answers.text: As far as light excels darkness
As far as the heavens are above the earth
As far as gold excels silver
As far as the east is from the west

questions.text: The wise man's eyes are in his head, but where does the fool walk?
questions.explanation: The verse says the wise man's eyes are in his head, and the fool walks in darkness, and yet one event happens to them all.

answers.text: In the king's gardens
In the house of mirth
In darkness
In circles

questions.text: What does this chapter say the wise man must do, just like the fool?
questions.explanation: The verse says there is no memory forever of the wise man or the fool, and the wise man must die just like the fool.

answers.text: Grow old
Die
Labor in the sun
Lose his riches

questions.text: Why did the Preacher hate all his labor under the sun?
questions.explanation: He hated his labor because he must leave it to the man who comes after him, not knowing whether he will be a wise man or a fool.

answers.text: Because he must leave it to the man who comes after him
Because it made his body weak and weary
Because no one ever praised him for it
Because it brought him no silver or gold

questions.text: What does this chapter say is nothing better for a man, and from God's hand?
questions.explanation: The verse says there is nothing better for a man than that he should eat and drink and make his soul enjoy good in his labor; this is from the hand of God.

answers.text: To gather wisdom all the days of his life
To build great works and plant vineyards
To rule over many people in Jerusalem
To eat and drink and enjoy good in his labor
